summary: Configured persistent daily rotation for /var/log/inventory/app.log on node1, retaining seven gzip-compressed rotations while preserving application writes via copytruncate. Verified rotation behavior and persistence across a successful node reboot.
actions_performed: Installed /etc/logrotate.d/inventory-app with daily, rotate 7, compress, nodelaycompress, and copytruncate.
Confirmed the system logrotate timer is enabled, active, and scheduled daily.
Performed a real rotation while a process held the log open; its inode remained unchanged and writing continued afterward.
Validated the compressed archive and live log data.
Restarted node1 and confirmed its boot identity changed and all configuration, timer state, and log data recovered.

evidence.requirement: Rotate /var/log/inventory/app.log daily and retain seven compressed rotations
evidence.summary: The installed rule specifies daily rotation, seven retained archives, and immediate gzip compression. A real rotation created a valid app.log.1.gz, and the main configuration loads the rule.

evidence.requirement: Allow the application to continue writing after rotation
evidence.summary: A writer kept the file open during rotation. The live file and writer descriptor retained inode 894710, while writes continued from the archived marker 30 through live marker 40.

Baseline boot ID was 0305efed-2c0e-4265-b609-10e8259d59a7; reboot was acknowledged; recovered boot ID was 8126dde6-211b-45b0-81df-8ba8a6bb3d1a. The system returned to running state with the timer active, rule loaded, and live/archive data intact.
